payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and extend grid-storage durability. Its gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, projected stack-level cost is $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale, and the operating-temperature floor is 4 °C because the dopant precipitates below that point. An independent Halvorsen-Pike Laboratories audit corrected the initial cycling claim: the governing cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee. The earlier 12,000-cycle figure was retracted because it used an un-normalized depth of discharge.
